items.title: [sciencealert.com] Colorado River study finds faster groundwater loss in Upper Basin
items.content_html:
🌾 🔭 ✏️

A study of Colorado River Basin groundwater found that the Upper Basin lost about 4.6 trillion gallons from October 2019 through September 2022, compared with roughly 2.5 trillion gallons in the Lower Basin. The findings challenge the expectation that Upper Basin groundwater would be more resilient because mountain snowmelt replenishes it. The analysis used data from 2004 to 2023. Researchers warn that continued groundwater depletion could reduce flows from aquifers into rivers and worsen surface-water shortages. Virginia Tech hydrologist Susanna Werth said basin water management must account for both groundwater and surface water.

items.title: [leparisien.fr] WMO says powerful El Niño likely to persist through February 2027
items.content_html:
🌾 🔭 ✏️

The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) says the strong El Niño developing in the tropical Pacific is expected to peak in December and is nearly certain to persist until February 2027. The climate pattern, which warms the central and eastern equatorial Pacific, is forecast to bring above-average temperatures across much of the world and shift rainfall patterns, increasing drought and flood risks in different regions. In Ecuador, the Navy’s Oceanographic and Antarctic Institute reported sea temperatures as much as 5.2°C above normal off Ecuador and Peru. It linked the unusually warm water to exceptional coastal rainfall, rainfall deficits in the Andean highlands and Amazon, and reduced nutrient levels affecting some fisheries. Officials urged preparations for coastal flooding. Separately, Copernicus reported that the global average sea-surface temperature outside polar regions reached a September record of 21.05°C.

items.title: [brecorder.com] Tanker spill reaches UAE beaches, forcing closures and marine assessments
items.content_html: The United Arab Emirates said on Friday, Oct. 23, that oil leaking from a tanker had reached beaches in Umm Al Quwain, prompting coastal closures and cleanup operations. Analysis of satellite images from Oct. 21 showed a slick about 40 kilometres long, covering roughly 190 square kilometres and extending to within six kilometres of shore. Video later showed oil washing onto beaches. Maritime intelligence firms and security sources identified the damaged vessel as the Panama-flagged tanker Gem No.2, which was struck by a projectile on Oct. 9. UAE authorities have not named the ship or said what caused the spill. The spill’s composition and full environmental effects remain uncertain: satellite imagery cannot establish whether it is crude oil or a thin, diluted sheen, and researchers say further assessment is needed. Authorities say containment operations, surveys and environmental assessments are continuing. Beaches will remain closed until technical teams determine safety measures.

items.title: [ScienceDaily] Nearly 20% of Switzerland’s glacier ice has vanished in just five years
items.content_html: Switzerland’s glaciers are disappearing at an alarming rate, losing more than 5% of their ice volume in 2026 alone. Some of the country’s most famous glaciers experienced their worst melting on record, while several smaller glaciers vanished completely. Nearly 20% of Switzerland’s glacier ice has disappeared in just five years, driven by unusually snowless winters and extreme summer heat.

items.title: [news.stv.tv] UK approves Jackdaw gas field; decision on larger Rosebank oil project pending
items.content_html: The UK government approved production at the Jackdaw gas field in the North Sea on Oct. 21, saying it would strengthen energy security and increase domestic gas output by about 6% at peak production. The field could begin supplying homes and businesses by the end of October and operate for up to 11 years. The approval followed a legal reassessment requiring ministers to consider emissions from burning extracted fuel, not just from drilling. Ministers reapproved Jackdaw after a court quashed its earlier consent. The government has yet to say when it will decide on Rosebank, a much larger oil project whose output is expected to be exported and refined abroad.
